row.name: EUROPEAN RIVER CRUISE w/ HH SOCIAL
row.full_description:
EUROPEAN RIVER CRUISE w/ HH SOCIAL is an eight day journey that follows the Rhine river through the heart of Europe. The route includes Cologne, Germany and Basel, Switzerland, two cities with their own distinct character and charm. This is a river cruise, so you can settle in and watch the scenery drift past between stops. A travel specialist can help you plan this trip around what you enjoy most.

Cologne sits on the Rhine river in North Rhine-Westphalia. It is one of the nation's media, tourism and business hotspots, and is considered one of the most liberal cities in Germany. The city has a rich history, reaching back to the time of the ancient Roman Empire, when it was founded. Along the way you might explore its old city gates and historic buildings, or simply wander and take in the atmosphere of a place with so many layers of the past.

Basel is one of Switzerland's underrated tourist destinations. It has a beautiful medieval old town centre, a fascinating carnival, and several art museums built by notable architects. Basel is also rich in architecture old and new, with a Romanesque Münster cathedral, a Renaissance Rathaus town hall, and various examples of high quality contemporary architecture. Located in the Dreiländereck, the three countries' corner, Basel is a gateway to the Swiss Jura mountains and nearby cities of Zürich and Lucerne, as well as the neighbouring French region of Alsace and the German Black Forest.

Between these two cities, the Rhine threads its way through landscapes that have drawn travellers for generations. A river cruise lets you unpack once while the view keeps changing. You can spend your days ashore discovering old towns, museums and riverside corners, then return to the comfort of the ship. It is a relaxed way to see this part of Europe without the rush of packing and moving between hotels.

Basel Old Town is compact, which makes it easy to explore on foot. You could visit the Kunstmuseum Basel or the Museum Jean Tinguely, step inside the Elisabethenkirche, or bring the family to Basel Zoo. In Cologne, the city's gates and churches tell the story of its long history, from the Hahnentorburg to the Severinstorburg and the Basilica of the Holy Apostles.

This kind of trip suits anyone who loves a blend of scenery, history and culture, with the ease of travelling by water. Whether you are drawn to Cologne's ancient roots or Basel's mix of medieval streets and modern art, there is plenty to discover along the Rhine.

If an eight day European river cruise from Cologne to Basel sounds like your kind of getaway, a travel specialist can help you plan this. Ask about this trip and start a conversation about dates, details and what matters most to you. We can help you plan something that fits the way you like to travel.

Related: [Germany](/destinations/germany).

row.name: CROATIA COASTLINE YACHT CRUISE
row.short_description: Dubrovnik, Slano, Korcula, Vis, Bisevo, Hvar, Stari Grad, Boi, Split, Trogir, Sibenik, Vodice, and Zagreb
row.full_description:
CROATIA COASTLINE YACHT CRUISE invites you to explore the Adriatic coast of Croatia over 12 days. This is a cruise that traces some of the loveliest shores and islands in the Mediterranean. The route includes Dubrovnik, Slano, Korčula, Vis, Biševo, Hvar, Stari Grad, Boi, Split, Trogir, Šibenik, Vodice, and Zagreb. Along the way you can discover walled towns, marble streets, fishing harbours and quiet island bays.

Dubrovnik is a historic walled city on the Adriatic Sea coast in the extreme south of Croatia. Nicknamed the Pearl of the Adriatic, it is a seaport and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. You can wander past Big Onofrio's Fountain, step through the Pile Gate and admire the Rector's Palace and the Church of Saint Blaise.

Slano is a village in southern Croatia with a small harbour in the bay of the same name. Korčula is a Croatian island known for Grk, a white wine that is only produced on the island. Biševo is a Croatian island in the Adriatic Sea, a peaceful place to pause along the coast.

Hvar feels remarkable, with imposing fortifications hovering above grey stone and orange roofs. Its marble streets reveal one of the largest squares in Dalmatia and the prized Cathedral of St. You can climb up to the Španjola Fortress for views over the brilliant blue sea. Stari Grad shares the same beautiful Dalmatian character of walls, promenades and quaint harbours.

Split is a city in Central Dalmatia built around the Diocletian palace, where locals sought refuge centuries ago. Wandering the historic centre you can still clearly see the Roman walls, squares and temples. Visit the Peristylium, stroll the Riva promenade and explore the Basement halls of Diocletian's Palace. Trogir is a medieval town and a popular day trip from Split, home to the Kaštel Kamerlengo.

Šibenik rewards slow walks, with the Fortress of St and gardens to explore, plus beaches around Šibenik for a swim. Vodice sits nearby along the same stretch of coast. Zagreb, the capital of Croatia, has a charming medieval old city with architecture and cobbled streets reminiscent of Vienna, Budapest and Prague. There you can see the Zagreb Cathedral, the Old Town Gate and the Museum of Broken Relationships.

This trip blends time on the water with time ashore, so you can enjoy both the sea and the towns that rise above it. The waters of the Adriatic, the island vineyards and the stone streets all come together into one memorable journey. It suits travellers who love history, coastal scenery and the easy rhythm of cruising from port to port.

If this sounds like the kind of holiday you have been imagining, a travel specialist can help you plan this. Ask about this trip and share what you hope to see. We can help you plan the details so the journey feels right for you.

Related: [Croatia](/destinations/croatia).
